name: Cabin (pollen) filter
summary: Replace the cabin-air filter and verify airflow. Renault directs the owner to the vehicle maintenance schedule for filter intervals.
interval: Follow the vehicle maintenance document; exact interval not stated in the fetched handbook page.
safety: Do not force brittle trim or cover clips.

parts.name: Cabin filter

specs.label: Replacement interval
specs.notes: Use the maintenance schedule for this vehicle and market. Mégane III handbook value removed; Mégane II value not yet sourced.

removal.text: Switch off the ignition and identify the cabin-filter access panel for this dashboard and left-/right-hand-drive configuration.
Release the access cover without bending its tabs, then withdraw the old filter while noting its airflow direction.

installation.text: Clean loose debris from the housing without pushing dirt into the HVAC duct.
Fit the correct filter in the marked airflow direction, secure the cover, and test blower operation.

checks: Confirm the cover is fully seated and there is no bypass gap.
Check airflow and listen for debris in the blower.

name: Wiper blades
summary: Renew blades that no longer clear the glass cleanly. The owner handbook gives a replacement method and an approximate annual interval, but not blade lengths.
interval: About every year, or sooner if wiping effectiveness declines.
safety: Never let a bare wiper arm fall onto the glass.
Do not run blades on a dry windscreen.

parts.name: Front wiper blades
Rear wiper blade

specs.label: Front and rear blade lengths
specs.notes: Not specified in the fetched handbook page; verify by VIN/body style and existing connector.

specs.label: Replacement interval
specs.notes: Mégane III handbook value removed; Mégane II value not yet sourced.

removal.text: With the ignition on and engine stopped, place the front wipers in the service position using the stalk; switch off the ignition.
Lift an arm, release its blade latch and slide the blade off. For the rear blade, pivot it away from the glass and release its latch as fitted.
removal.warning: Protect the glass and hold each arm; an unloaded arm can strike and crack the glass.

installation.text: Slide each correctly matched blade onto its arm until the latch engages.
Lower the arms gently and test the wipe on a wet screen; confirm each blade locks and parks correctly.

checks: Check for streaking, chatter, missed areas and secure end locks.

name: Wiper motor and linkage
summary: Diagnose the fuse, supply, linkage and motor before replacement. Access and linkage indexing vary by body and equipment; use the VIN-specific service method.
safety: Keep hands clear of linkage while powered.
Disconnect the battery before disturbing motor wiring.

parts.name: Wiper motor or linkage assembly

removal.text: Park the wipers, switch off the ignition and disconnect the battery using the vehicle electrical procedure.
Remove the cowl trim and wiper arms as required, keeping track of clips and drain seals.
Unplug the motor and separate the linkage only as required; note its parked orientation before removal.

installation.text: Install the linkage and motor in their parked position; route the harness clear of moving arms.
Reconnect the battery and test a full wipe cycle before reinstalling the cowl and arms.

checks: Confirm correct park position, sweep, speed settings and washer coordination.
Check that the cowl drains and seals are restored.

faults.causes: Check power supply, fuse, connector, seized linkage and motor before replacing parts.

name: Windscreen washer pump
summary: Check fluid, blocked jets, hose routing and pump power before replacing the washer pump.
safety: Avoid spilling washer fluid onto paint or electrical connectors.

parts.name: Washer pump and seal

removal.text: Switch off the ignition and identify the reservoir and pump access for the exact body style.
Protect paintwork, disconnect the pump connector and hose, and catch fluid before releasing the pump.

installation.text: Fit a sound seal and pump, reconnect hose and electrical plug, then refill with suitable washer fluid.
Operate the washer briefly and confirm spray direction and leak-free connections.

checks: Check both front and rear washer circuits where fitted.
Clear blocked jets without enlarging their orifices.

faults.causes: Empty reservoir, frozen fluid, blocked jets, split hose, fuse, wiring or pump failure.

name: Headlamp bulbs
summary: The repair manual lists halogen bulb designations, but access differs by engine and may use the wheel-arch flap, engine bay or headlamp removal. Confirm the fitted lamp by VIN.
safety: Never energise a lamp outside its housing.
For xenon equipment, do not handle the high-voltage lamp/ballast; use the dedicated procedure and qualified service.

parts.name: Replacement bulb matching the fitted headlamp

specs.label: Main beam
specs.notes: Use only an approved bulb; equipment varies by vehicle.

removal.text: Identify whether the car has halogen or xenon lamps and find the access route for the fitted engine and headlamp.
Switch off the lights, remove the appropriate rear cover and release the bulb connector and retainer.

installation.text: Fit the matching approved bulb without touching its glass, secure the retainer and refit the cover.
Test the lamp and confirm the beam aim has not shifted.

checks: Verify left/right operation and correct high/low beam function.
Have headlamp aim checked after disturbing the lamp assembly.

name: Headlamp unit
summary: Headlamp assemblies differ by halogen/xenon and trim. Xenon-equipped systems require special precautions and system initialisation after replacement.
safety: Disconnect the battery before headlamp work.
Xenon ignition is hazardous; never energise a removed lamp and do not dismantle a hot ballast.

parts.name: Headlamp assembly matched to VIN and lighting option

specs.label: Lamp technology and actuator serviceability
specs.value: Halogen and xenon variants exist; xenon levelling actuator is not separately removable from the projector.

sources.title: Renault Mégane II workshop manual (manuelmeg.org)— manuelmeg.org reproduction
sources.locator: Xenon system safety, battery disconnection, cool ballast; actuator is not separately removable

sources.title: Renault Mégane II workshop manual (manuelmeg.org)— manuelmeg.org reproduction
sources.locator: Xenon and halogen headlamp removal methods are identical; initialise and aim xenon system after fitting

removal.text: Disconnect the battery and allow any xenon ballast assembly to cool before work.
Remove the required front trim or bumper access pieces, unplug the lamp connectors and release the unit fixings.
Withdraw the lamp without loading its wiring or damaging adjacent bodywork.

installation.text: Install the matching assembly, connect the harness and restore all seals and trim.
For xenon variants, initialise the system and adjust headlamp aim after installation.

checks: Test all functions, levelling and warning indicators.
Check beam alignment and water ingress.

name: Rear lamp bulbs
summary: Rear lamp bulb type depends on body style and lamp equipment. Confirm the marked bulb or VIN catalogue before replacement.
safety: Use the correct bulb type and wattage for the installed unit.

parts.name: Rear lamp bulb matched to the installed unit

specs.label: Rear lamp bulb designations
specs.notes: Not verified for every Mégane II body and lamp option.

removal.text: Switch off the exterior lights and open the relevant luggage-compartment access.
Release the lamp carrier or service cover according to the installed unit; do not pull on wiring.
Remove the failed bulb using its carrier lock and note its orientation.

installation.text: Fit the exact matching bulb and lock the carrier into the lamp.
Reconnect and test tail, stop, indicator and reversing functions as applicable.

checks: Check all rear lamp functions and that the lens seal is correctly seated.

name: Number-plate lamp
summary: Inspect the lens, connector and bulb type before replacement; equipment varies by market and body style.
safety: Avoid levering against painted surfaces with a bare metal tool.

parts.name: Number-plate lamp bulb or lamp assembly matched to vehicle

specs.label: Bulb designation
specs.notes: Not confirmed for the full model/body range.

removal.text: Switch off the exterior lights and protect the paint around the lens.
Release the lens or lamp with a suitable trim tool and disconnect the bulb holder.

installation.text: Fit the matching bulb or assembly, reconnect it and seat the lens seal evenly.
Switch on the lamps and verify the plate is illuminated.

checks: Confirm the lens is secure, dry and evenly illuminated.

name: Front fog lamps
summary: The workshop-manual method removes the front bumper to access the fog lamps, then removes their fixings; refit and adjust the beam afterward.
safety: Support the bumper during removal to avoid damaging paint or wiring.

parts.name: Fog lamp matched to vehicle equipment

specs.label: Post-installation adjustment
specs.value: Adjust the fog-lamp beam after refitting.

sources.title: Renault Mégane II workshop manual (manuelmeg.org)— manuelmeg.org reproduction
sources.locator: Remove front bumper and fog-lamp fixing screws; refit in reverse and adjust with screwdriver

removal.text: Protect the bumper finish and remove it using the body-specific service procedure.
Remove the fog-lamp fixing screws and withdraw the lamp; disconnect its connector if needed.

installation.text: Reconnect and secure the lamp, then refit the bumper in reverse order.
Adjust the fog-lamp beam with a screwdriver and verify operation.

checks: Check lamp operation, beam direction and bumper fastener engagement.

name: Fuse boxes and fuse identification
summary: Fuse assignments and box locations vary with equipment and production version. Use the vehicle-specific handbook or fuse-card markings; no complete K4M fuse map was verified.
safety: Never bridge a fuse or fit a higher rating.
Disconnect the battery before working on exposed wiring.

parts.name: Replacement fuse of the exact specified rating

specs.label: Fuse-box locations and circuit map
specs.notes: Verify against the exact vehicle handbook and fuse-card; not confirmed in this research.

removal.text: Switch off the affected circuit and ignition, then consult the fuse-card or vehicle handbook for the correct fuse.
Remove the fuse with the puller and inspect it; do not substitute a different rating.

installation.text: Install only a fuse matching the specified rating and refit the cover securely.
Test the circuit; if the replacement fuse opens again, stop and diagnose the fault.

checks: Confirm the repaired circuit works and the fuse does not open again.

name: Horn
summary: Check the fuse, relay/control path, wiring and horn unit before replacing the horn. Access may require front bumper removal.
safety: Do not work near the steering-wheel airbag or its wiring during horn diagnosis.

parts.name: Horn unit matched to vehicle

removal.text: Switch off the ignition and disconnect the battery before accessing the front harness.
Locate the horn, unplug its connector and inspect for corrosion, water ingress or damaged wiring.
Release the mounting fastener and remove the horn if testing confirms failure.

installation.text: Install the correct horn, reconnect the connector and secure the harness away from moving or hot parts.
Reconnect the battery and test the horn.

checks: Check horn operation and that its sound is not obstructed.

name: Door mirror glass
summary: Mirror glass can include heating or blind-spot equipment. Match replacement glass to the installed option and use a body-specific removal method.
safety: Wear eye protection and gloves when handling broken mirror glass.

parts.name: Mirror glass matched to vehicle options

specs.label: Heating and monitoring options
specs.notes: Confirm against the VIN and existing mirror connector.

removal.text: Position the mirror for access, protect the housing and release the glass evenly with a plastic tool.
Disconnect any heater or monitoring connectors without pulling their wires.

installation.text: Reconnect option-specific terminals and align the glass with the backing plate.
Press evenly around the centre until retained, then test adjustment and heating if fitted.

checks: Check glass retention, adjustment, heating and warning-system operation if fitted.

name: Crankshaft position sensor
summary: Diagnose the sensor circuit and connector before replacement. Access, sensor configuration and fastener data must be checked against the engine/VIN-specific repair information.
safety: Keep hands and leads clear of belts and rotating components.

parts.name: Crankshaft position sensor and seal, as applicable

removal.text: Allow the engine to cool, switch off the ignition and disconnect the battery.
Locate the sensor using K4M-specific service data, release its connector and inspect the harness.
Remove the retaining fastener and withdraw the sensor without damaging its seating face.

installation.text: Clean the seating area, fit the correct sensor and seal, and secure it using the verified K4M procedure.
Reconnect the harness, clear codes if required and verify starting and engine-speed signal.

checks: Check for stored engine-speed signal faults and confirm reliable hot/cold starting.

faults.causes: Possible sensor, connector, wiring, supply or related engine-management fault; confirm with diagnosis.

name: Coolant temperature sensor
summary: Identify the K4M sensor by VIN and diagnostic data. Replacement may open the cooling system, so use a cold-engine procedure and restore coolant level and bleeding.
safety: Never open the cooling system hot.
Keep coolant away from children and animals.

parts.name: Coolant temperature sensor and seal, as applicable

specs.label: Coolant capacity
specs.notes: Not established for this K4M vehicle configuration.

sources.title: Renault Mégane II workshop manual (manuelmeg.org)— manuelmeg.org reproduction
sources.locator: K4M listed for the water-box bleed point; cold/temperate coolant protection shown as −20 C ±2

removal.text: Let the engine cool completely and relieve system pressure only when safe.
Identify the sensor from K4M-specific information, protect nearby electrical parts and catch escaping coolant.
Disconnect the plug and remove the sensor without damaging its port.

installation.text: Fit the correct seal and sensor, refill as required, then bleed the cooling system using the vehicle-specific method.
Reconnect the sensor and check live temperature data, leaks and coolant level after cooling.

checks: Confirm stable temperature reading and no leaks.
Recheck the coolant level after a complete cool-down.

name: Oil pressure switch
summary: An oil-pressure warning can indicate a real lubrication failure; check oil level and pressure before condemning the switch.
safety: Do not continue driving with a genuine low-oil-pressure warning.

parts.name: Oil pressure switch and sealing washer, as fitted

removal.text: If the oil-pressure warning is on with the engine running, stop the engine and check oil level before further operation.
Switch off, allow hot parts to cool, disconnect the switch connector and verify the fault with suitable pressure testing.
Remove the switch while preventing dirt from entering the oil passage.

installation.text: Install the correct switch and seal using verified K4M service data; reconnect the plug.
Start only after checking oil level, then verify the warning extinguishes and inspect for leaks.

checks: Confirm actual oil pressure when a warning or pressure fault is present.
Check switch connector and sealing for oil leaks.

name: Ignition key/card battery
summary: Card/key battery type and opening method vary by key-card generation. Confirm the marking and replace without damaging the case or circuit board.
safety: Keep coin cells away from children; do not short or swallow a battery.

parts.name: Key-card battery matching the fitted card

specs.label: Battery type and orientation
specs.notes: Not verified for the different Mégane II card generations; read the fitted battery marking.

removal.text: Work on a clean, dry surface and identify the exact key-card version.
Open the case at its intended seam and note the battery polarity before removal.

installation.text: Fit a fresh battery of the identical type with matching polarity, then close the case without pinching the seal.
Test remote locking and starting; follow the owner handbook if re-synchronisation is needed.

checks: Check button response and passive start/recognition where equipped.

name: Air-conditioning system service
summary: Refrigerant type, charge mass and compressor oil quantity must be read from the vehicle label or VIN-specific service data; none was confirmed here. Refrigerant recovery and charging require qualified equipment.
safety: Do not vent refrigerant or open a charged system.
Use trained personnel and appropriate eye/skin protection.

parts.name: Refrigerant and compressor oil as specified on vehicle label

specs.label: Refrigerant type
specs.notes: Verify on the vehicle label; do not assume by model year.

removal.text: Inspect the system and identify the refrigerant label before connecting service equipment.
Recover refrigerant with approved equipment; do not vent it or loosen a charged line.
Only disconnect components after recovery and follow the specified oil balancing procedure.

installation.text: Replace seals as required, evacuate and charge only to the vehicle-label specification.
Check for leaks, compressor operation, vent temperature and diagnostic faults.

checks: Confirm no leaks and stable system operation.
Record recovered and charged amounts against the label specification.

name: Radiator cooling fan
summary: The cooling fan may start unexpectedly. Diagnose fan supply, control and wiring before removal; access and control strategy vary by equipment.
safety: The fan can start without warning; keep hands clear even with the ignition off.
Protect radiator fins from tools.

parts.name: Cooling fan or fan assembly matched to vehicle

removal.text: Switch off ignition, allow the engine to cool and isolate the battery before working near the fan.
Unplug the fan, release the shroud and wiring retainers, then remove the assembly without damaging the radiator.

installation.text: Seat the fan and shroud correctly, secure the harness away from blades and reconnect the plug.
Reconnect the battery and confirm fan operation using a safe diagnostic activation or controlled operating check.

checks: Check fan clearance, connector security and cooling performance.

name: Front bumper removal
summary: Bumper removal is required by the workshop-manual fog-lamp procedure. Fastener layout differs by trim and body, so confirm the correct body-specific method before pulling the cover.
safety: Use a second person to support the bumper.
Do not pull against connected wiring.

parts.name: Replacement bumper clips, if damaged

specs.label: Fog-lamp access
specs.value: Remove the front bumper to access the front fog lamps.

sources.title: Renault Mégane II workshop manual (manuelmeg.org)— manuelmeg.org reproduction
sources.locator: Remove front bumper and fog-lamp fixing screws; refit in reverse and adjust with screwdriver

removal.text: Protect painted edges and disconnect the battery if unplugging powered lighting or sensor equipment.
Release wheel-arch, lower-edge and upper-edge retainers using the body/trim-specific procedure.
With an assistant supporting the cover, disconnect fog lamps or other fitted harnesses and remove the bumper without forcing it.

installation.text: Reconnect all lamps and sensors, align the bumper guides and engage retainers without trapping wiring.
Check all joints, clips and electrical functions; adjust fog lamps if disturbed.

checks: Confirm bumper gaps are even and all retainers engage.
Test fog lamps and any fitted front sensors.

name: Door trim panel
summary: Door-trim fasteners and clips depend on door and equipment. Protect trim and isolate the battery before working near side-airbag wiring or powered equipment.
safety: Do not probe or disturb airbag connectors.
Use non-marring tools to avoid damaging clips and trim.

parts.name: Door-panel clips, replace if damaged

removal.text: Switch off ignition and disconnect the battery if the work involves airbag or electrical connectors; follow the restraint-system wait and handling procedure.
Remove the trim caps and fasteners appropriate to the exact door, then release the panel clips progressively.
Lift the panel clear and disconnect handles, switches and speakers without pulling on wires.

installation.text: Reconnect components and verify switch operation before aligning the panel.
Engage the clips evenly, reinstall fasteners and confirm the moisture barrier remains sealed.

checks: Check door lock, window switch, speaker and handle operation.
Confirm the trim is flush and the moisture barrier is intact.
